tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on the symptomatic/user-facing triggers (error messages, failure modes) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts (RHUI cert expiry, subscription lapses, GPG/NOKEY errors, proxy issues, NTP skew, specific error strings) including the case where 'the user only says the repos are unreachable', and is a concise single paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Linux EC2 instance's patching is blocked by a repository access or authentication failure ... even when the user only says the repos are unreachable.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific fault classification, exact diagnostic commands, and recovery ordering without explaining general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., it doesn't explain what GPG or TLS are generally).
tests.evidence: RHUI client cert expired (RHEL PAYG): certs in /etc/pki/rhui/ are region-specific (~2-year validity).

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps diagnosis to a short bash snippet and routes detailed fix commands to separate reference files rather than embedding large reference tables or lookup data inline.
tests.evidence: RHUI cert / RHUI repo failure → read [rhui certs](reference/rhui-certs.md).

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (RHUI cert reinstall, order of clock/auth/CA/metadata fixes) are given exact prescriptive steps, while diagnosis routing explains reasoning (why GPG failures may really be cert issues) giving the agent room to reason — appropriately calibrated.
tests.evidence: Correct the clock first if skewed — a wrong system time fails TLS cert and metadata-signature validation and makes every other symptom worse.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple package managers/approaches are relevant, the skill lists the applicable one per OS/mechanism rather than presenting equal menus, and routes to specific reference docs based on diagnosed cause.
tests.evidence: `dnf clean all` + `makecache`, `apt-get update`, `zypper refresh` — only after the auth/cert fix, or you just re-cache the failure.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic and recovery procedure (classify fault → route to reference → fix in order → verify) applicable to any instance/OS, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the access fault before changing anything... Step 2: Route to the fault (load the matching reference for exact commands)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this domain (region-specific RHUI certs, clock skew masquerading as cert expiry, etc.).
tests.evidence: RHUI certs are region-specific. An instance launched from an AMI copied to another region has the wrong RHUI cert...

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: This is primarily a diagnostic/recovery procedural skill rather than a report-generation skill; it doesn't require a structured output template beyond the validation checklist already present.
tests.evidence: The skill's purpose is diagnosis and recovery of repo access, not a formatted report deliverable.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output templates exist in the body; the content is diagnostic/procedural rather than a report skeleton.
tests.evidence: No templates present in the body — passes by absence.
